newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Central African Republic diamond bourse reopens.
newsitem.headline: Central African Republic diamond bourse reopens.

text.p: Diamond dealing resumes on Central African Republic's (CAR) bourse on Wednesday after being suspended since June 1996 after fighting stemming from an army pay dispute, a government source said on Tuesday.
The bourse was set up in February 1996 but trading was suspended after sessions in March, April and June.

Sales in those months' sessions added up to around 5,200 carats valued at 7OO million CFA francs ($1.13 million), said the source, adding that CAR's annual diamond production totals around 500,000 carats.
Smuggled diamonds accounted for up to 50 percent of official CAR diamond production, a mines official at the commodities ministry said.
